newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL share index falls two pct on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: KL share index falls two pct on weak sentiment.

text.p: The benchmark Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's Composite Index fell two percent in late afternoon trade as market sentiment remained weak after overnight losses on Wall Street and credit tightening measures announced by Bank Negara last week, dealers and analysts said.
At 0818 GMT, the index was down 23.69 points or 2.01 percent to 1,157.38, its lowest level in five-and-a-half months.
Dealers said shares were pulled down by lack of support from funds and calls by broking houses to clients who had bought shares on credit to top up their margins.
"There's a lot of margin calls," said Tony Shue, an institutional dealer at Jupiter Securities.
Banking and property stocks again led the fall on worries of the central bank curbs on property and share buying.
By 0815 GMT, market volume stood at 274 million shares, with losers overwhelming gainers 644 to 44.
